sources: SATURDAY Oct 3 2026 RUN (06:12 UTC, weekend - all market fields are Friday Oct 2 closes or Oct 1-2 official prints). HEADLINE: THE LABOUR MARKET CRACKED. SEPTEMBER PAYROLLS +29K, UNEMPLOYMENT 4.2 PCT, SAHM RULE BACK TO ZERO - AND THE OIL SHOCK RESTARTED. THE LABOUR DATA - THE WHOLE STORY OF THIS RUN: September nonfarm payrolls +29,000 against a +90,000 consensus, the weakest print of the cycle; unemployment rate 4.2 pct, up from 4.1 pct; August revised DOWN to +133,000 (BLS Employment Situation, released Oct 2 12:30 UTC). Yahoo Finance quotes labour demand as 'flashing yellow'. For eleven consecutive runs this dashboard flagged that the market was pricing a hiking Fed into soft survey data with a labour market that had not yet cracked. It cracked on Oct 2. SAHM RULE - THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT NUMBER ON THE DASHBOARD TODAY: 0.00 for September (FRED SAHMREALTIME, released Oct 2 13:36 UTC), UP from minus 0.07 in August and the first non-negative print of this cycle. The Sahm rule triggers at +0.50, so 0.00 is not a recession signal - but the sign flip is the first time the three-month average unemployment rate has stopped falling relative to its twelve-month low. Direction, not level, is the information. Next print Nov 6. FED REPRICING - VIOLENT: bond traders cut the odds of an OCTOBER Fed HIKE to about 20 pct, from 64 pct one week earlier (Yahoo Finance, Oct 2). The Oct 1 run had this at 38 pct and falling; it has now effectively been priced out. Mohamed El-Erian: the weak data puts 'the Fed definitely on hold for October.' Eleven runs of a hiking path being priced reversed in a single session. CREDIT - EIGHT STRAIGHT SESSIONS: ICE BofA US High Yield OAS 312bp (FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2, 3.12 pct dated Sep 30), an EIGHTH consecutive session of widening. Full sequence: 268 (Sep 18), 266 (Sep 21), 268 (Sep 22), 273 (Sep 23), 280 (Sep 24), 293 (Sep 25), 302 (Sep 28), 308 (Sep 29), 312 (Sep 30) - 44bp with not one day of retracement. Credit widened BEFORE the labour data arrived; this is the eighth run in a row it has been the cleanest stress signal here, and it now has a fundamental to point at. OIL - THE SHOCK RESTARTED: Brent 102.25 USD/Bbl (TradingEconomics, Oct 2), versus 97.46 at the Oct 1 run and 95.87 at the Sep 30 low - plus 6.7 pct in two sessions. OilPrice.com has Brent 102.24 and WTI 92.62 on Oct 2. Drivers: the US sending a THIRD aircraft carrier to the Middle East (Brent jumped over 4 pct on Oct 1 on the report, CNBC), China halting all fuel exports for October, and Bloomberg NEF saying Hormuz disruption and the US blockade of Iran are 'likely to persist in some form into the new year'. Trump: Iran will 'sign a very fair deal, or they won't exist any longer'. The Sep 16-30 round trip from 127.84 to 95.87 is now partly retraced; the war premium is rebuilding. Trend up. EQUITY VOL FELL ON THE BAD NEWS: VIX 15.31 (Cboe, Oct 2 close), DOWN 6.59 pct from 16.39, and equities RALLIED on the weak payroll print - S&P 500 plus 0.73 pct, Nasdaq plus 1.19 pct. Bad news is good news again because it kills the hike. This is the first run in which equity vol and credit spreads have pointed in opposite directions, and it is worth watching which one is wrong. BOND VOL OFF THE RECORD: MOVE 105.74 (TradingView TVC-MOVE, Oct 2), minus 1.06 pct on the day from the 106.61 record, but still plus 14.5 pct over one week and plus 45.1 pct over one month. Trend up. RATES: 2s10s 0.46 (FRED T10Y2Y, Oct 1), up from 0.41 (Sep 30), 0.37 (Sep 29) and 0.26 (Sep 23) - 20bp of bear steepening in six sessions and the steepest of the episode. IMPORTANT: this FRED print is dated Oct 1, BEFORE the payroll report, so the curve field does not yet contain the labour reaction. Yahoo Finance has the 10y dropping to 5.18 pct on Oct 2 on the jobs data, while TradingEconomics still shows 5.28 pct as of Oct 2 - treat the 10y as unresolved between 5.18 and 5.28 and expect the Monday curve print to move. BREAKEVENS STILL ANCHORED: 5y5y forward 2.36 pct (FRED T5YIFR, Oct 1), unchanged from Sep 29 and versus 2.34 on Sep 22. Brent has now round-tripped 30 dollars DOWN and 6 dollars back UP and long-run inflation expectations have moved 2bp in three weeks. Tested in both directions twice; has not broken. FINANCIAL CONDITIONS STILL ASLEEP: NFCI minus 0.548 for the week ending Sep 25 (FRED NFCI), no new release at run time - sequence minus 0.560 (Sep 4), minus 0.558 (Sep 11), minus 0.553 (Sep 18), minus 0.548 (Sep 25). Three consecutive weeks of microscopic tightening, total half a basis point of index, against a 44bp HY move and a record MOVE. Conditions remain at the loosest of the cycle. Carried as flat. The divergence is now five weeks old and is the main unresolved question on this dashboard. DOLLAR: DXY 101.92 (TradingEconomics, Oct 2), DOWN 0.17 pct on the day on the weak employment data but up about 2.1 pct on the month and at the highs of the year. Trend up over one week. COPPER/GOLD 1.57, up from 1.56. Copper 6.492 USD/Lbs (plus 0.75 pct) and gold 4,140.19 USD/t.oz (MINUS 0.90 pct), both TradingEconomics Oct 2; 6.492/4140.19*1000 = 1.568. Gold fell and copper rose on the weak jobs print, which is the opposite of the growth-scare reaction and fits the kill-the-hike trade. Roughly flat over one week. Global liquidity 1 (stable). REAL ECONOMY - SOFT ACROSS THE BOARD: ISM manufacturing 54.5 for September (ISM, released Oct 1), DOWN from 54.6 in August, with PRICES PAID surging to 77.9 - still expansionary but decelerating with cost pressure building, the stagflationary mix. Initial claims 197k for the week ending Sep 26 (FRED ICSA, fresh print), UNCHANGED from the prior week and still historically low - the one indicator that has NOT confirmed the payroll weakness, and the key thing to watch next Thursday. UMich consumer sentiment 48.1 (final September, confirmed via Advisor Perspectives, minus 7.0 pct / 3.6 points from 51.7 in August, a four-month low, one-year inflation expectations 4.6 pct). Building permits 1,403k (August, next release Oct 20). LEI 99.5 for August with six-month growth of minus 0.1 pct (Conference Board Sep 2026 release); y/y carried at about minus 0.7 pct. CARRIED STANDING ASSUMPTIONS, no free live source: SOFR-OIS 0bp, EUR/USD 3M cross-currency basis minus 10bp. BDTI DATA FLAG - TWELFTH consecutive run carried at 4,899 and formally non-informative. Investing.com remains frozen at 1,107 dated 31/03, Barchart and MacroMicro inaccessible, Baltic Exchange subscription-only, lowdown.today last refreshed 18 May. Public commentary puts the real BDTI all-time high near 1,900 points (May 2026), so 4,899 is not on a comparable scale and must not be read as a level. Wire a paid source or drop the tile. PICTURE: this is the run the dashboard has been waiting for. For eleven sessions the signal was a market pricing a hiking Fed into deteriorating surveys with an intact labour market, and credit widening for reasons nobody could pin down. On Oct 2 the labour market delivered: +29k payrolls, unemployment to 4.2 pct, August revised down, and the Sahm rule off negative for the first time. The October hike was priced out within hours, equities rallied, gold fell and the dollar slipped. Credit, which had already widened 44bp over eight sessions with no explanation, now looks prescient rather than idiosyncratic. The complication is that the oil shock restarted in the same week - Brent back over 102 on a third US carrier and a Chinese export halt - so the Fed is being handed a weakening labour market and a fresh energy impulse simultaneously, with ISM prices paid already at 77.9. That is the stagflation trap, and broad financial conditions have registered none of it. WATCH: whether initial claims (next Thursday) confirm the payroll weakness or keep contradicting it - 197k is not a cracking labour market; whether HY OAS makes it nine sessions or finally retraces now that it has a fundamental; whether the NFCI print this week finally turns up after five weeks of divergence; whether the 10y settles at 5.18 or 5.28 and where 2s10s prints Monday; whether MOVE holds above 100; whether Brent takes 105 and re-establishes the war premium; and ISM services plus CPI as the next tests of the prices-paid impulse.
